entries.v: The Heirloom of Kldekari
Grigol Kldekareli's sword. Brass wire in the fuller reads ✠ ႵႤ ႸႤ ✠, "Christ, have mercy". The house kept two things: the tower and this.
Monaspa sword
The royal guard's double-edged sword, forged to one pattern: the monaspa must look as one.
Frankish sword
A broad blade and a straight crossguard. It came from Antioch; heavy, but it opens a shield.
Kipchak sabre
A lightly curved blade for cutting from the saddle. Kipchaks wrap the grip in horsehair.
Flanged mace
Iron flanges crack mail and lamellar alike. It needn't be sharp.
War axe
A highlander's axe: one winter it splits firewood, the next, shields.
Infantry spear
An ash shaft and a leaf-shaped head. It means more in a line than in a hand.
Kipchak composite bow
Horn, wood and sinew, glued; it hates damp. Its case hangs on the left hip.
Dagger (satevari)
A short double-edged dagger. It is in the hand before the sword is drawn.
Lamellar
Hundreds of iron plates laced in rows with rawhide. When one breaks, the rest hold.
Tevdore's lamellar
Banded, riveted lamellar, as the warrior saints wear it in the churches of Svaneti.
Mail hauberk
Riveted rings to the knee. It turns a cut, not a blow: wear padding under it.
Quilted jacket
Two layers of linen with cotton or wool between. A townsman's armour and a soldier's underlayer.
Wool qaba
A front-opening wool coat, slit for the saddle.
Monaspa Crimson
A madder-crimson coat over lamellar. The whole guard wears one colour: from afar, everyone knows whose they are.
Fur cloak
A hide cloak, fur inside. Kakhaber sleeps in his; nobody asks to borrow it.
Segmented helmet
A helmet riveted from segments, with a mail curtain over the neck.
Conical helmet
Raised from a single piece of iron. A blow slides off the point.
Splinted vambraces
Iron strips on leather, laced round the forearm.
Mail leggings
Mail for the legs, when the shield is high.
Leather boots
Tall riding boots. In snow they last two days; on the third your feet find out.
Long shield
A long shield that covers a rider to the knee. Bakur's bears the gold vine cross on black.
Round shield
A round, hide-faced shield. Handier in a lane than a long one.
Mother's enkolpion
A bronze cross of two hinged halves. Inside is something holy his mother never told him about.
Father's ring
A carnelian ring with a cut sign. He pressed it into the wax when his name was not on the list.
Tone bread
Baked on the wall of a clay oven, eaten hot.
Sheep's cheese
Trialeti shepherds' cheese, kept in brine.
Red wine
Kakhetian red in a wineskin. In Lent, only on Saturdays and Sundays.
Churchkhela
Walnuts on a thread, dipped in thickened grape must.
Pomegranate
From the city's gardens, picked before the siege.
Honey
In a clay pot. In war, honey goes on wounds too.
Yarrow
It stops blood, Bakur's mother used to say.
St John's wort
Steeped in oil, it heals wounds.
Savory
Lentil stew wants savory, says Giorgi the Cook.
Linen bandage
Boiled linen. Clean, which in a camp is rare.
Wound salve
Wax, honey and herbs. Eliezer says the wax keeps the air out of a wound.
Road rations
Bread, cheese, dried fruit and an onion, wrapped in cloth.
Whetstone
A grey stone that hangs from the belt. A few strokes before a fight and the edge bites again.
The Sword's Answer
An old monaspa master's notes.
The Shield Wall
A book of the line.
The Steppe Bow
Kipchak archery, written down in Georgian.
The Cry of Didgori
Written the day after the battle.
The Peerless Karabadini
A Georgian book of healing.
The Strategikon
A Greek book of war.
Bodkin arrow
A narrow four-sided head, made for a mail ring.
Icon of St George
In a chased silver frame. The host carries such icons before it.
Glazed bowl
A Tiflis potter's bowl with green glaze. Its potter is somewhere behind the wall.
The Keys of Tiflis
Keys on an iron ring. Heavier than they look.
The King's Letter
For Sioni's priest, under the king's seal. Bakur doesn't know what it says; he knows what he promised.
Bale of silk
City silk, packed under a merchant's mark: the same mark he saw on the envoys' bales.
The first page: "First receive, then return. Whoever tries both at once loses both."
The first page: "Your shield guards the man on your left. His guards you."
The first page: "The horse breathes out: you loose. One arrow does not need two breaths."
The first page: "A war cry is not for the enemy. It is for your own: so they hear you are still standing."
An eleventh-century Georgian book of healing: herbs, oils, fevers and wounds.
About a hundred Frankish knights stood in King David's host. They brought their own swords.
A Greek book of war: how to fight horse-archers, and how not to chase them when they run.
Vardan's Forge
The camp's forge: swords, axes, spears and shields. Vardan sings while he hammers.
Good morning, Kldekareli. The forge is still cold. My hand isn't.
You're early. In winter even iron wakes slowly.
Come, come. Stand by the fire before we talk money.
Evening work has a bad name. But for you, I'll forge.
I'm named for Vardan Mamikonian. He lost his battle and kept his church. Not a bad trade.
Quickly, aznauri. I'm banking the forge.
Kldekareli. Got money? I sell to a traitor's son for money, like anyone.
People talk. Iron doesn't. What do you need?
I saw your father's sword once. A good sword. Of the man I say nothing.
Your priest won't give me the bread. Your sword doesn't mind my steel.
Come. I've kept my best iron for you.
My brother still shoes the emir's horses in Ani. One day your king will want my brother's iron too.
That rusty axe you sold me last time, I couldn't even make a horseshoe of it.
What are you bringing today, Kldekareli? More rust?
You took the money, I took the rust. We can't trade like that.
Straight and double-edged, the way Georgians like it. The weight sits by the guard: the hand won't tire.
I've rewound the grip in new linen. The old one smelled of blood.
A mace doesn't need a clever man. It needs a strong one.
A flange bends the lames, and under them the man's bone breaks.
A highlander's axe. The haft is ash, not lime: it won't break.
It hooks a shield and drags it down. Then the man is yours.
A spear teaches two things: distance and patience.
It's cheap, because a line needs many.
A dagger is the last word. The last word should be short.
Keep it in your boot. At night in camp, not everyone is a brother.
Riders love a long shield. On foot it's heavy, but it keeps you alive.
Hide stretched over twice. An arrow goes in halfway and stops.
A round shield is for lanes: it needs no room to turn.
The townsmen carry these. We'll see whose is better.
Fine. The iron wants to go with you more than I want to keep it.
So be it. I'll finish my song and regret it after.
So be it. I beat the steel; I can't beat you.
Neither yours nor mine.
Put one silver on top and it's yours.
Shall we shake on it? No. Money first.
I haven't that much in my purse, Vardan. I'll give you what I have.
The whole camp will see this and ask whose work it is. Count that in the price.
Half. I'll put it in your hand right now.
No. This iron came from the mountains of Armenia, not from your purse.
For half the price I'll give you half a sword. Want it?
That price is lower than my singing. No.
Copper on copper. A good sound.
As much as it's worth. No more.
Put it on the anvil. That's better.
Silver! In this camp I guard silver like fire.
You count it. I listen to the sound.
For this you'd buy a horse. You chose a sword. Rightly.
I'll wrap it in cloth so the rust doesn't take it.
Try it. Cut the air. You see?
Oil it every week. If you forget, the rust will remind you.
God make your sword true and your shield hold.
Come back alive. A dead buyer pays me nothing.
Go. The forge is calling me.
It's a sharakan, our hymn. It isn't like yours, but God hears both.
The hammer needs the song's beat. Without it the iron has doubts.
My father hammered like this in Ani. Exactly like this.
It's night, Kldekareli. Even the iron sleeps.
In the morning. My hand would slip now.
…All right, come in. But you'll pay a fifth more.
